containerRules: Numeric columns and rows use minmax(0,1fr) tracks with zero intrinsic minima on root and items.
Responsive columns and rows emit scoped viewport media rules and preserve a non-responsive sibling axis.
minColumnWidth uses CSS auto-fit and min(100%, value), adapting natively to host width.
Consumer inline style is final except responsive axes deliberately clear their engine inline template so media rules can own that axis.
invariants: dir is forwarded; named areas and numeric lines remain authored CSS semantics in RTL.
Grid owns no pointer, touch or keyboard navigation model; role and tabIndex do not synthesize ARIA grid behavior.
Long content cannot force fractional tracks beyond their assigned share without an explicit consumer template.

transitions: Grid.Item placement has no family-owned transition

entries: Grid and Grid.Item keep stable root identity through track and placement changes.
Responsive projection clears only the axis owned by responsive CSS.
Numeric gaps and track dimensions never emit NaN, Infinity or negative gap geometry.
Item span and line normalization omits invalid zero and non-finite placements while preserving legal negative lines.
Theme controls never choose columns rows spans areas ordering or interactive semantics.
Unset tenant controls must exactly restore root attributes, channels, tracks and computed gaps.

A preset gap attribute is engine-owned output, never consumer input. RECORDED HAZARD, pre-existing and now shared by three attribute names (data-gap-preset, data-column-gap-preset, data-row-gap-preset): the base rules keyed on those attributes are not engine-scoped, while Classic and Rustic forward caller data-* props through extractSemanticDOMAttributes. A caller who hand-stamps one of them on a Classic or Rustic grid produces var(<unset>), which is invalid at computed-value time and collapses the gap to normal. The Modern engine strips a hand-stamped attribute from a numeric axis, so the exposure is Classic and Rustic only. Engine-scoping is one decision that must be taken for all three names at once.
